title: The Big Picture Discussion Group
description: What's the function of art in Society? Can art save the world? Come gather at Venue 515 on The Business of Art Center campus every Wednesday night from 6 to 8 PM as we attempt to uncover the truth about art and its place in the world. What are the spiritual benefits, if any, to art? How has religion influenced art and vice-versa? All religious practices and artistic disciplines are respected. Everyone is welcome. The idea is to build community through dialogue. This is a structured discourse with a different facilitator each week. The discussion group will also have guest speakers, occasional movies and critiquing sessions. Bring your art, your thoughts, and your ideas. Let's talk about it.

title: Ranger Guided Programs at Florissant Fossil Beds National Monument
times: Park hours are 8 a.m.-6 p.m. in summer and 9 a.m.-5 p.m. otherwise.
tickets: The fee to enter the park is $3 per person for anyone 16 years or older (15 years or younger are free).
description: A variety of ranger guided programs will be offered throughout the summer which includes ranger talks, guided walks, science demonstrations at an excavation site, a fossil discovery lab and much more. Please call ahead for times and schedules. The junior ranger program, park film and exhibits, two self-guided trails, and 14 miles of hiking trails are available to visitors throughout the year. Please contact the Monument at (719) 748-3253 for further information about hours and the schedule for programs.

title: Cheyenne Mountain Zoo
times: Extended summer hours: 9 a.m.-6 p.m. All other times: 9 a.m.-5 p.m.
tickets: Adults: $14.25 Seniors: $12.25 Children 3-11: $7.25 Children 2 and under: Free
description:
An opportunity to get in tune with the animal in us all is always available at the Cheyenne Mountain Zoo! Featuring unique exhibit spaces including the new Rocky Mountain Wild exhibition, the zoo is a showcase for perennial family favorites like giraffe feeding, peacock plumage preening, wallaby wonderment, monkey madness and let's not forget the spectacular views of the city offered by Cheyenne Mountain Zoo's unique position as the nation's only mountain zoo!

A little background information: The Cheyenne Mountain Zoological Society was founded in 1926 by philanthropist Spencer Penrose to house his growing collection of exotic animals. In 1938, after substantial development, Mr. Penrose incorporated the Zoo as a non-profit public trust for the people of Colorado Springs “for the sole purpose of establishing and maintaining a zoological park to provide recreation, education, conservation, and scientific facilities in the field of zoology and related subjects, and to preserve the Zoo in perpetuity for the people of the Pikes Peak region.”

title: Artist Trading Card Sessions
description: Artist Trading Cards, known as ATC's, are masterpieces in miniature that artists around the globe are creating and trading with each other. ATC's are 2.5"x3.5" original works of art in any media. The cards are traded and not sold. You don't have to be an artist or artistically inclined to participate. All you need is some card stock and a little creativity. A few supplies will be provided. A different presenter will be featured each month (sponsored by Concrete Couch) and from 12-2 p.m., there will be free soup and a trading session sponsored by Pikes Peak Arts Council.

title: Rocky Mountain Wild at the Cheyenne Mountain Zoo
times: Extended summer hours: 9 a.m.-6 p.m. All other times: 9 a.m.-5 p.m.
tickets: Adults: $14.25 Seniors: $12.25 Children 3-11: $7.25 Children 2 and under: Free
description: As America’s only mountain zoo, Cheyenne Mountain Zoo is uniquely suited to showcase Rocky Mountain wildlife in its natural setting. The Rocky Mountain Wild exhibit complex connects you with the wild heritage of the Rocky Mountain region–offering surprising, engaging and memorable encounters with moose, mountain lions, North American river otters, lynx, bald eagles and grizzly bears.
